challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to .faff/ at all, not only committing them; gitignore does not address that rule. The new decision writes resolved API keys in plaintext to .faff/cache/credentials.json, so they persist on disk after the session, can be swept into backups, archives or support bundles, and outlive key rotation. The claimed benefit (avoiding process.env reads) is negligible, since env access is an in-memory lookup and an in-process cache would give the same gain without a file. The argument does not show the old rationale has stopped holding; the supersession is unsound.
